qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the Delaware Division of Public Health for professional services related to the Delaware Health Fund. It includes a procurement schedule, submission deadlines, evaluation criteria, and contract terms, clearly indicating a procurement opportunity.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
Delaware Health Fund – FY 2028 Health Programs and Services
This request for proposals (“RFP”) is issued pursuant to 29 Del. C. §§ 6981 and 6982.
Date: September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT
This RFP is open to private organizations.

findings.title: Response to Questions Posted
findings.fact: The Department's response to questions will be posted by September 3, 2026.

quotes.quote:
Response to Questions Posted by:  
Date: September 3, 2026

The Department’s response to questions will be posted, according to the procurement 
schedule, under the project listing in Euna Procurement (formerly Bonfire) and to the State 
of Delaware Bid Solicitation Directory Website: http://www.bids.delaware.gov/ by 
September 3, 2026.

findings.title: Evaluation Period
findings.fact: Evaluation of proposals is scheduled from September 15 to October 9, 2026.

quotes.quote:
Evaluation of Proposals  
Date: September 15 – October 9, 2026

findings.title: Draft Recommended List Posted
findings.fact: The draft recommended award list will be posted publicly no later than October 15, 2026.

quotes.quote:
Draft Recommended List Posted Publicly:   
Date: October 15, 2026

Notice of Award: Please read carefully.  Selection under this RFP results in placement on the 
Division’s draft recommended award list, which will be posted publicly no later than October 15, 
2026, reviewed by the Health Fund Advisory Committee at a public meeting with public 
testimony no later than November 7, 2026, and transmitted as a final recommended award list 
to the Governor, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, the Controller General, 
and the members of the Joint Finance Committee no later than November 15, 2026.  Funding is 
contingent upon appropriation by the General Assembly in the Fiscal Year 2028 appropriations 
act, and recommended awards are subject to amendment by the Joint Finance Committee 
through the budget process.  No contract or grant agreement will be executed, and no funds will 
be paid, unless and until such appropriation is enacted; contracts for funded awards are 
anticipated to begin July 1, 2028.  Recommended amounts may differ from requested amounts, 
and final appropriated amounts may differ from recommended amounts.

findings.title: Proposal Firm Offer and Property of State
findings.fact: Proposals become the property of the State of Delaware at the proposal submission deadline and are considered firm offers at that time.

quotes.quote:
Proposals become the property of the State of Delaware at the proposal submission 
deadline.  All proposals received are considered firm offers at that time.

findings.title: Evaluation Start Time
findings.fact: Evaluation of proposals is expected to begin shortly after the proposal due date.

quotes.quote:
Evaluation  of  the  proposals  is  expected  to  
begin shortly after the proposal due date.

findings.title: Mandatory Attachments and Forms
findings.fact: Offerors must complete all appropriate attachments and forms as identified within the RFP to be eligible.
findings.business_implication: Failure to complete all required attachments and forms will render the proposal non-responsive and may lead to disqualification, regardless of the quality of the technical proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Create a compliance checklist of all required attachments and forms from the RFP and verify each is completed and included before submission. Have a second person review the submission for completeness.

quotes.quote: 3. Complete all appropriate attachments and forms as identified within the RFP.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Proposals must be submitted by September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT.
findings.business_implication: Late proposals will not be accepted under any circumstances. The submission is electronic via the Euna Procurement portal, and the system will reject submissions after the deadline. This is a hard deadline with no exceptions.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to submit well before the deadline to avoid last-minute technical issues. Test the portal in advance, ensure all files are uploaded and the final submission is clicked, and retain the confirmation email as proof of timely submission.

quotes.quote:
Deadline for Receipt of Proposals  
Date: September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT
All proposals must be submitted prior to 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026.

a.   Proposals must be received before the Proposal Due Date and Time, as 
identified in the Procurement Schedule for this RFP.  
Responses received after the Proposal Due Date and Time will not be accepted.

Any  proposal  submitted  after  the  Deadline  for  Receipt  of  Proposals  date  will  not  be  
accepted.

Proposals submitted after the specified date and time will not be accepted by the Euna 
Procurement  (formerly  Bonfire)  Portal.    Evaluation  of  the  proposals  is  expected  to  
begin shortly after the proposal due date.  To document compliance with the deadline, 
the  proposal  will  be  date  and  time  stamped  upon  receipt  by  Euna  Procurement  
(formerly Bonfire).

The  State  of  Delaware  will  receive  proposals
  via Euna  Procurement  (formerly  
Bonfire)
 until the date and time shown in this RFP.

findings.title: Deadline for Questions
findings.fact: Questions must be submitted by August 28, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST.
findings.business_implication: Questions submitted after this deadline may not be answered, and clarifications may not be provided in time to influence the proposal. This could lead to misunderstandings and a non-compliant proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly and submit all questions through the designated portal before the deadline. Monitor the Q&A section for responses and incorporate any clarifications into the proposal.

quotes.quote:
Deadline for Questions  
Date: August 28, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST
Questions may be submitted no later than August 28, 2026 @ 3:00 PM EST.

findings.title: Deadline for Notifying State of Discrepancies
findings.fact: Vendors must notify the State of any discrepancies, omissions, or ambiguities at least ten (10) days before the proposal opening.
findings.business_implication: Failure to notify the State of any perceived errors or ambiguities in the RFP within the specified timeframe may result in the waiver of the right to protest based on those issues. This could put the bidder at a disadvantage if the RFP contains errors that affect the proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review the RFP for any discrepancies, omissions, or ambiguities and notify the designated contact in writing at least ten days before the proposal opening. Document all communications and retain copies.

quotes.quote:
Should vendor find discrepancies, omissions, unclear or ambiguous intent or 
meaning, or should any questions arise concerning this RFP, vendor shall notify the 
State of Delaware’s Designated Contact, in writing, of such findings at least ten (10) 
days before the proposal opening.

Protests based on any omission or error, or on the content of the solicitation, will be 
disallowed  if  these  faults  have  not  been  brought  to  the  attention  of  the  Designated  
Contact, in writing, at least ten (10) calendar days prior to the time set for opening of 
the proposals.

findings.title: Contract Term and Renewal
findings.fact: The contract term is one year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation; continued funding is subject to annual statutory process and appropriation.
findings.business_implication: The contract is for one year only and does not guarantee renewal. Funding for subsequent years is subject to a separate annual appropriation and RFP process. This creates uncertainty for long-term planning and may require the bidder to reapply each year.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for a one-year contract and consider the need to reapply in subsequent years. Prepare a strong proposal for the initial term and be prepared to participate in future RFPs to continue the program.

quotes.quote:
1.   Contract term is one (1) year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, 
contingent on appropriation.  Funding in subsequent fiscal years is not a renewal right: 
continued funding is subject to the annual statutory process under 16 Del. C. § 137(i), 
including the annual request for proposals, and to annual appropriation.  Organizations 
funded in Fiscal Year 2028 that seek Fiscal Year 2029 funding must respond to the Fiscal 
Year  2029  RFP  (anticipated  release  on  or  before  July  1,  2027),  which  is  expected  to  
include  a  streamlined  continuation  response  for  organizations  proposing  to  continue  
substantially the same program.

findings.title: General Evaluation Requirements
findings.fact: Proposals will be evaluated based on six criteria: Statement of Need, Alignment with Health Fund Priorities, Program Design and Feasibility, Measurable Outcomes and Evaluation Plan, Organizational Capacity & Past Performance, and Budget Reasonableness and Sustainability.
findings.business_implication: The proposal must comprehensively address all six evaluation criteria to be competitive. Strong emphasis is placed on direct ties to tobacco prevention/cessation and cancer prevention/detection/treatment, and on sustainability given declining Master Settlement Agreement revenue.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the proposal explicitly addresses each criterion with Delaware-specific data, clear program design, measurable outcomes, evidence of organizational capacity, and a realistic budget that accounts for funding sustainability. Highlight any direct alignment with tobacco and cancer priorities.

quotes.quote:
B.  General Evaluation Requirements  
1.   Statement of Need (§ II.A of proposal)-Delaware-specific evidence of the health need 
and the service gap the program fills; for returning organizations, including prior-year 
results. 
2.   Alignment  with  Health  Fund  Priorities  (§  II.B)-fit  with  the  purposes  in  16  Del.  C.  §  
137(d), with the strongest weight for direct ties to tobacco prevention and cessation 
and to cancer prevention, detection, and treatment. 
3.   Program  Design  and  Feasibility  (§  II.C)-goals,  activities,  timeline,  staffing,  and  
geographic reach that are specific, coherent, and achievable within the contract year. 
4.   Measurable Outcomes and Evaluation Plan (§ II.D)-specific, verifiable objectives with 
indicators,  targets,  and  data  sources,  suitable  for  incorporation  into  the  award  
agreement. 
5.   Organizational   Capacity   &   Past   Performance   (§   II.E)-governance,   financial   
management, audit history, and experience operating programs of similar scope. 
6.   Budget  Reasonableness  and  Sustainability  (§  II.F)=  justified  costs  proportionate  to 
reach,  documented  other  funding,  and  a  realistic  plan  given  declining  Master  
Settlement Agreement revenue.

findings.title: Right to Refuse Proposals
findings.fact: The Proposal Evaluation Team reserves the right to refuse to consider any proposal from a vendor who meets certain unspecified conditions.
findings.business_implication: The State has broad discretion to reject proposals based on unspecified conditions, which introduces uncertainty. Vendors must ensure compliance with all stated requirements and maintain a clean record to avoid disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the full list of exclusion criteria in the RFP (e.g., criminal convictions, ethical violations) and ensure the organization has no such issues. Maintain documentation of past performance and ethical conduct to demonstrate responsibility.

quotes.quote:
The Proposal Evaluation Team reserves the right to refuse to consider any proposal 
from a vendor who:

findings.title: Acceptance of Exceptions
findings.fact: Acceptance of exceptions is within the sole discretion of the evaluation committee.
findings.business_implication: Any exceptions to the RFP terms and conditions are not guaranteed to be accepted; the evaluation committee has sole discretion. This means that proposing exceptions may put the bid at risk if they are not approved.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review the RFP terms and conditions before submitting. If exceptions are necessary, clearly document them on Attachment 4 and be prepared for the possibility that they may be rejected. Consider whether the exceptions are essential or if the proposal can be submitted without them.

quotes.quote:
Acceptance of exceptions is within the sole discretion of 
the evaluation committee.
